newFeatures: Export: new Output sharpening (Sharpen for Screen, Matte paper or Glossy paper; Low, Standard or High), off by default. It sharpens only the exported file after resizing, and adapts to the print resolution or to how much the photo is downsized.
Export: new Resolution setting (pixels per inch, default 300) under Size, written into the exported file.
] and [ give a photo one star more or less, and Shift+0–5 sets the rating and moves to the next photo, as in Lightroom (Library, culling, Compare and Survey).

Photos added before 0.4.0 now get their GPS location and, if their camera preview is Adobe RGB, thumbnails with correct colours, once, in the background (with Pause); edited photos, ratings and sidecars are left as they are.
bugFixes: On keyboards with accented letters (German Ü, Ö, Ä; French é, è, ç, à), those keys no longer act as the US key in the same place (e.g. Ctrl+Ä made a virtual copy).
Virtual copies now keep their photo's GPS location.

newFeatures: Lens corrections: distortion, chromatic aberration and dark corners are corrected with the camera's own data (Sony, and Fujifilm, Olympus, DNG and Panasonic as darktable reads them) or a Lensfun profile. On for new photos; earlier edits stay as they were until you tick Lens corrections.
The Lens section (in Crop & Lens) shows which data corrected the photo, lets you pick the camera or lens when the match is wrong, and has Distortion and Vignetting amounts.
Lensfun's lens data is downloaded the first time a photo needs it, then works offline.

Transform: Upright Auto, Level, Vertical and Full straighten leaning buildings and tilted horizons in one click, using darktable's line detection and the photo's focal length; when the lines found aren't reliable, the photo is left alone and LightBench says why.
Guided Upright (Shift+T): draw 2–4 lines along edges that should be vertical or horizontal; drag their ends to adjust, Delete removes one.
Transform sliders: Vertical, Horizontal, Rotate, Aspect, Scale and X/Y Offset. The photo is enlarged so no empty corners show.
Auto straighten in the crop group (or double-click with Level on) levels the photo along the lines it finds.
Paste, Sync and presets: Upright Auto, Level, Vertical and Full are detected again on each photo; the Transform sliders are copied as they are.
A JPEG shot alongside a RAW now keeps its own sidecar (IMG_1.JPG.xmp), so the two no longer share stars and edits.
Thumbnails and previews of RAWs shot in Adobe RGB show their real colours instead of looking washed out.
Where a photo was taken (GPS) is read from RAWs and JPEGs and shown in the Library's info panel.
Title, caption, creator, copyright, location and keywords written by older apps (IPTC) are read from JPEGs.
On wide-gamut (Display P3) screens, Develop shows colours beyond sRGB.
Fujifilm X-Trans RAW files (RAF) now open, develop and export, with darktable's Markesteijn demosaic.
Linear DNGs (Apple ProRAW and other phone or converter DNGs) now open, develop and export, using the colour matrices stored in the file.
bugFixes: Extreme Tint or Temp settings on a JPEG no longer turn its colours inside out (e.g. Tint +150).
Phone DNGs whose camera LibRaw doesn't know (e.g. Google Pixel) no longer fail with “Matrix is not invertible”.

newFeatures: Crop and straighten (R): drag corners or edges, drag inside to move, drag outside to turn the photo under a level crop box. Enter applies, Esc cancels.
Crop aspects Original, 1:1, 4:5, 5:7, 2:3, 16:9 and Custom, with a lock; X swaps portrait and landscape; O cycles thirds, grid, golden ratio and diagonals.
Straighten with the Angle slider, or draw a level line along the horizon (the Level button, or Ctrl-drag while cropping).
Rotate left and right (Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+]) and flip horizontally or vertically.
The crop is used everywhere: histogram, Auto, thumbnails, Export, 100 % views, and Paste, Sync and presets (tick Crop to copy it).
Develop's tools are now one scrolling list with a jump bar (Crop, Basic); groups can be closed, and an eye shows the photo without a group.
Process versions: each edit remembers which version of LightBench's rendering it uses, so later changes never alter it until you choose “Update to current process”.
Back up the whole library (catalog, thumbnails and settings) to one checked file, and restore it safely.
LightBench notices when Lightroom, darktable or another app changes a photo's sidecar, and asks before overwriting it.
bugFixes: Star ratings changed in Lightroom or Bridge are no longer overridden when LightBench re-reads the sidecar.
Keywords that other apps store only as plain (flat) keywords are no longer dropped.
Photos copied from a card are now checked byte-for-byte; a bad copy is reported instead of being added.
A library saved by a newer LightBench is refused untouched, with a Reload button.
Notices when the browser may clear the library, or when a save fails.

newFeatures: Compare (C): the photo you like best stays on the left while the arrow keys bring in others to compare with it.
Survey (N): the selected photos side by side, to flag, rate and drop them until the best are left.
Metadata: edit title, caption, creator, copyright and location on one photo or many. They are saved in sidecars and included in exports.
Metadata presets (“© {year} Your Name” becomes each photo's year) that can fill in new photos, and import presets for the Import window's options.
Settings (the gear, or Ctrl+,): change any keyboard shortcut, or switch to Lightroom Classic's keys.
Press ? for the shortcuts of the current view, or Ctrl+Shift+P to find any action by name.
Interface size from 90 % to 150 % (Ctrl+Alt+= and Ctrl+Alt+−). Photos stay sharp.
Choose the background behind photos: black, dark grey or mid grey.
Develop sliders: arrow keys nudge, Shift+arrows take bigger steps, Home resets.
Install LightBench as an app from Chrome or Edge (the install button in the address bar).
Works offline after the first visit. Your photos and library were already stored on your computer.
An “Update ready” notice with these notes. Nothing changes until you click Reload.
Open RAW and JPEG files with the installed app from your file manager (Chrome and Edge).
Copy, paste and sync develop settings between photos, choosing which settings go. Auto can re-run on each photo.
Auto options: a strength slider and a choice of which sliders Auto may change.
Presets: save chosen settings, preview on hover, apply with an Amount, and develop new photos with one automatically.
